paper.title_en: Quantum Gravity from Fractal Entanglement Geometry
paper.abstract_en: In this work, we explore the possibility that spacetime geometry may emerge from the entanglement structure of an underlying quantum-information network. We develop an exploratory framework, termed Fractal Entanglement Quantum Gravity (FEQG), in which information-theoretic correlations provide a candidate pregeometric structure from which aspects of geometry, quantum dynamics, and gravity may arise. An information-based distance on the correlation graph is considered as a possible means of relating quantum correlations to geometric separation. The framework also investigates whether scale-dependent and fractal properties of the underlying structure could lead to dimensional flow, potentially approaching an effective dimension of two near the Planck scale. Within a scale-relativistic perspective, nondifferentiable trajectories and stochastic descriptions are examined as possible ingredients in an effective quantum dynamics; however, the emergence of the Schrödinger equation from the network structure remains to be established. Similarly, the relation between evolving correlations and gravitational dynamics is explored through candidate generalized field equations, while recovering Einstein gravity in an appropriate macroscopic limit remains an open problem. Potential phenomenological consequences include dimensional reduction, modifications to gravitational potentials, and possible deviations from standard quantum mechanics at ultrashort scales. These possibilities are not presented as established predictions, but as directions for further investigation. FEQG thus provides a research program for examining whether quantum-information structure, fractal geometry, and gravitational phenomena can be connected within a common framework.
